Country.evidence_source: The present study is included in an ongoing investigation about the relationship between several psychological processes and positive body image indicators in Portuguese women and female adolescents (named "#KindGirlsInACTion").

Sample.evidence_source: Since the online questionnaire protocol was intentionally designed to only allow subjects who met criteria for inclusion to participate in the study, and the used survey app does not allow blank responses, all subjects who completed the questionnaires were included in the study, resulting in a sample of 288 women.

female.evidence_source: Same as overall sample: '...all subjects who completed the questionnaires were included in the study, resulting in a sample of 288 women.'

total.evidence_source: Same as overall sample: '...resulting in a sample of 288 women.'

Survey method.evidence_source: Participants were recruited online, i.e., by email invitations and through a social media (Facebook) while using the Exponential Non-Discriminative Snowball Sampling method (Heckathorn, 2011). An Internet link in invitations redirected potential participants to an online version of the questionnaires (using LimeSurvey, an on-line statistical survey web app).

section_summary.extract_value: This section describes a single study of Portuguese women (aged 18–55) recruited online via email and Facebook using an exponential non-discriminative snowball sampling procedure, with data collected through an online LimeSurvey questionnaire and ethics approval obtained. All respondents who completed the protocol were included, yielding N = 288; Table 1 reports means, SDs, and intercorrelations (including BMI M = 23.93 and BAS-2 correlated with BMI = -0.30).
